description.narrative: Design & monitoring. Socio-economic benefits are embedded across Components 1–4 and tracked in Annex C (Results Framework) with sex/age-disaggregated indicators. Baselines are set in Y1; progress reported in PIRs, MTR, and TER. Key benefits (with targets): · Green jobs & incomes. ~1,800 new jobs by 2030 (nurseries, park/corridor O&M, compost/biochar, e-mobility); =40% women/youth; SMIG-compliant wages; 3,000 informal drivers formalized (licenses, insurance, coop profit-share). · Women’s economic empowerment & leadership. =50% women/youth on 25 co-management committees; 50%of new e-moto licenses to women/youth; 30% of green-roof rebates for women-led MSMEs. · Public health. PM2.5 -20% in pilot corridors; UHI -1.5–2°C in target quartiers; flood-days -20% in priority wards ? lower household loss/downtime. · Access & inclusion. +1 m² accessible green space per capita for 1.5M low-income residents; safer, gender-responsive parks (CPTED, lighting, toilets). · Mobility & affordability. ~40% cross-lagoon travel-time reduction via solar water-bus; predictable, affordable swap tariffs for commuters. · Local enterprise growth. ~US$4m in NbS/green-roof/landscaping contracts to local SMEs; circular-economy revenues help fund O&M. Co-benefit illustrations. · Lake Nokoué ecotourism cluster (Avlékété): community-run kiosks, guides, and mangrove tours (women/youth staffed). · Gender-responsive green spaces: lighting, sightlines, safe routes; Safetipin-style safety scoring in the app. · Short value chains: nurseries ? local plantings ? compost/biochar hub ? park O&M, keeping spending local.
